scenarios.name: restore_reappends_the_revocation
scenarios.pins: a workspace restore after a rollback: the host re-appends every PK-signed revocation it has seen as device.revoked with actor H, the embedded revocation verbatim

steps.note: from_seq and head must name the last event on disk
head is not the last event's
the owner's restore, seq 5, prev = from_seq's head
the host puts the revocation back at once

scenarios.name: reader_cannot_see_a_dropped_revocation
scenarios.note: NOT a valid restore. A log-only reader cannot see the dropped revocation (it is only in the abandoned tail and in host state), so it accepts these lines; the host must refuse this restore, because 5.10 accepts a workspace restore only if the host re-appends every PK-signed revocation it has seen at once. Consumers must not read this scenario as 'restore without re-append is ok'.
scenarios.pins: the same restore without the re-append: the abandoned tail held lena1's revocation, which the new chain no longer shows

steps.note: from_seq and head must name the last event on disk
head is not the last event's
the owner's restore, seq 5, prev = from_seq's head

scenarios.name: workspace_restore_blocks_an_abandoned_member_added
scenarios.note: model-only: no revocation is known to this host
scenarios.pins: a workspace restore lists the abandoned person-signed workspace events (here a member.added) and the engine refuses them per log

steps.note: the owner's restore lists the abandoned member.added
the abandoned member.added appended again: same id, signature and based_on, a new seq and host_sig

scenarios.name: ticket_event_may_not_name_the_restore_window
scenarios.pins: 5.10: a ticket event's ws_seq may name the last event of the restore window (the restore, then the host's device.revoked re-appends) but not the restore or an earlier re-append

steps.note: the host's re-append, seq 6: the last event of the window
the ticket event names the restore (seq 5), which is not the last event of the window
naming the last event (seq 6) is fine
